footerNote: Visa reports 'net revenue' of $11,633M; this page starts from gross revenue of $16,313M so the $4,680M of client incentives shows as a cost.
oneTimers: Severance costs of $563M (inside personnel expense) from Visa's drive for operational efficiencies — excluded from its non-GAAP results.

A litigation provision of $253M for the interchange multidistrict litigation (MDL) case and other legal matters ($237M flagged as the special item), also excluded from non-GAAP results. Non-GAAP net income was $6.3B ($3.32 per share).
otherDetail: Investment income and other gains of $150M, less $194M of interest expense — net −$44M.

segments.note: Fees for clearing and processing each transaction.

segments.name: International transaction revenue

segments.name: Other revenue

takeaways.text: Net revenue rose 14% to $11.6B — data processing +17%, service revenue +14%, international transactions +6% on cross-border volume +15%, and other revenue +45%. Processed transactions grew 10%.
takeaways.title: Every line grew

takeaways.text: Personnel costs jumped 41% because of $563M of severance charges as Visa reshapes its workforce — the main reason GAAP profit grew only 7% while revenue grew 14%. Non-GAAP EPS was $3.32.
takeaways.title: A big severance bill

takeaways.text: Client incentives — rebates paid to issuing banks and partners — rose 18% to $4.7B, about 29 cents of every gross revenue dollar. They grow fast because the biggest banks negotiate hard to stay on the network.
takeaways.title: Incentives keep climbing

verdict: Visa's net revenue rose 14% to $11.6B as payments volume grew 11% — but a $563M severance bill inside personnel costs held GAAP profit growth to 7%.
